text: Abbey Road came out in 1969 and is the last album the Beatles recorded together, even though Let It Be was released later. Side one is a set of separate songs, including "Come Together," "Something" and "Octopus's Garden," and it ends with the abrupt cut of "I Want You (She's So Heavy)." Side two opens with "Here Comes the Sun" and "Because," then runs through an eight-track medley that finishes with "The End." The very short "Her Majesty" closes the record. It is a good album to learn in chunks, because the structure is so clear.

album: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band
text: Released in 1967, Sgt. Pepper presents itself as a concert by a fictional band. It opens with the title track, hands the microphone to a character called Billy Shears for "With a Little Help from My Friends," and brings the title song back as a reprise at track 12. The album then ends with "A Day in the Life," which sits outside the concert frame. With 13 tracks and short gaps between songs, it is often cited as the point where the album became a designed work rather than a collection of singles.

Revolver (1966) has 14 tracks and changes style constantly. It opens with George Harrison's "Taxman," includes the string-quartet arrangement of "Eleanor Rigby" and the sing-along "Yellow Submarine," and ends with "Tomorrow Never Knows," built on tape loops and studio effects. It is useful for training your ear because almost every track sounds different from its neighbors, which gives each position its own identity. On the original vinyl, side one ends with "She Said She Said" and side two begins with "Good Day Sunshine," a handy split into two sets of seven.

Rubber Soul (1965) is often described as the album where the Beatles began to treat a full record as one statement. Its 14 tracks mix folk-influenced songs, such as "Norwegian Wood (This Bird Has Flown)," which features a sitar, with pop songs like "Drive My Car" and "Michelle." The album opens with "Drive My Car" and closes with "Run for Your Life." Songs like "Nowhere Man" and "In My Life" sit in the middle, which makes the second half a good place to test your memory.

The 1968 double album known as the White Album has 30 tracks and a plain white cover. It is the Beatles at their most scattered and their most free, moving from the rock of "Back in the U.S.S.R." and "Helter Skelter" to the acoustic "Blackbird," the sound collage "Revolution 9," and the lullaby "Good Night" that closes the set. Because it is so varied, it is one of the hardest Beatles albums to rebuild from memory, and one of the easiest to break into smaller chunks by mood.

Lemonade was released in 2016 alongside a film that divided the story into chapters, and its 12 tracks follow that emotional arc, from "Pray You Catch Me" through "Hold Up," "Don't Hurt Yourself" and "Sorry" to the closing "Formation." The music moves across rock, country, soul and hip-hop, with guests including Jack White and Kendrick Lamar. The record rewards being heard in order, because the shifts in mood are part of what it is saying, which also makes the sequence easier to remember than you might expect.

Beyoncé arrived without warning in December 2013, released all at once as a "visual album" with a video to go with each of its songs. It has 14 tracks in our game, beginning with "Pretty Hurts" and ending with "Blue." Along the way it covers glossy pop, slow-burning R&B and hip-hop, including "Drunk in Love" and "Flawless." Because it was designed to be watched and heard as one piece, the order has a clear shape: bold statements first, intimate songs toward the end.

Renaissance (2022) is a dance album drawing on house, disco and club music, and its 16 tracks are sequenced so that many of them flow into one another like a DJ set. It opens with "I'm That Girl," includes "Break My Soul" and "Cuff It," and closes with "Summer Renaissance." It was presented as the first part of a planned trilogy, which continued with Cowboy Carter. Hearing it in order is a very different experience from hearing the singles one at a time, and it is a good album to try if you like continuous mixes.

Cowboy Carter (2024) is the second part of Beyoncé's trilogy, following Renaissance, and it is the longest album in our catalog at 27 tracks. It draws on country, folk, rock and more, and it is framed like a radio broadcast, with interludes such as "Smoke Hour Willie Nelson" and "The Linda Martell Show" introducing sections. It includes a reworking of The Beatles' "Blackbird" and a version of Dolly Parton's "Jolene." Several titles use stylized spelling, like "Ameriican Requiem" and "Spaghettii," and the game lists them that way.

Blonde (2016) has 17 tracks and is one of the most admired albums of its decade. It came out in August 2016, a day after the visual album Endless. It opens with "Nikes" and closes with "Futura Free," and in between it drifts through short spoken pieces, quiet guitar songs and a reprise. Beyoncé appears on "Pink + White" and André 3000 on "Solo (Reprise)." The interludes and quiet moments depend on their position, which makes the album harder to rebuild than its size suggests.

Channel Orange (2012) was Frank Ocean's debut studio album, following the mixtape Nostalgia, Ultra. Its 17 tracks begin with "Start" and end with "End," which gives you two easy anchors. In between are songs like "Thinkin Bout You," "Sweet Life," "Super Rich Kids" and the long, multi-part "Pyramids." André 3000 appears on "Pink Matter." The album won the Grammy for Best Urban Contemporary Album and is a good example of how soul and R&B can tell stories across a full record.

The College Dropout (2004) was Kanye West's debut and has 21 tracks, including several skits that give it the feel of a school day. It features "Jesus Walks," "All Falls Down," "Slow Jamz" and "Through the Wire," the last of which he recorded while recovering from a jaw injury after a car accident. The album ends with "Last Call," a track of around twelve minutes in which he tells the story of his path to this record. With skits and a long closer, it has plenty of landmarks to hold on to.

Graduation (2007) has 13 tracks and trades the soul samples of Kanye West's earlier work for big, stadium-sized synths. It opens with "Good Morning" and ends with "Big Brother," and in between are "Stronger," which samples Daft Punk, "Can't Tell Me Nothing," "Flashing Lights" and "Homecoming." It was released on the same day as 50 Cent's Curtis, which turned into a much-discussed sales contest. With no skits and a steady pace, it is a clean album to practice on.

808s & Heartbreak (2008) is a short, stark album of 12 tracks, built on the Roland TR-808 drum machine that gives it its name. Kanye West sings through Auto-Tune instead of rapping, and the songs deal with loss and isolation. It opens with "Say You Will" and includes "Heartless," "Love Lockdown" and "Paranoid," and it ends with "Pinocchio Story." The record had a large influence on the pop and hip-hop that followed, and its sparse sound makes each track easy to tell apart.

My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy (2010) has 13 tracks and is known for its dense, layered production. It opens with "Dark Fantasy," includes "Power," "Monster," "Runaway" and the paired "All of the Lights (Interlude)" and "All of the Lights," and closes with "Who Will Survive in America," which features a spoken-word recording by Gil Scott-Heron. The album is long on ideas, with many guests and shifts in mood, but a strong order holds it together, so it rewards careful attention to what leads into what.

Yeezus (2013) is one of the shortest and harshest major albums in our catalog, with just 10 tracks. The production is abrasive and influenced by industrial and electronic music, and the packaging was equally stripped back, with no booklet or artwork on the case. It opens with "On Sight" and includes "Black Skinhead" and "New Slaves." It closes with "Bound 2," the warmest and most song-like track, which feels like a release after the tension. With only ten positions, it is a great album to start with in the game.

The Slim Shady LP (1999) was Eminem's major-label debut, released through Dr. Dre's Aftermath label. It has 20 tracks, including five skits, and features "My Name Is," "Guilty Conscience" and "Role Model." A quarter of the album is made up of short spoken pieces, which makes it one of the harder tracklists to learn, since skits are easy to forget and easy to confuse. The best strategy is to learn the songs first and then slot the skits in between them.

The Marshall Mathers LP (2000) followed the success of The Slim Shady LP and became one of the fastest-selling albums in US history at the time. It has 18 tracks, three of them skits, and includes "Stan," which is built around a sample of Dido's "Thank You," along with "The Real Slim Shady" and "The Way I Am." It opens with "Public Service Announcement 2000" and ends with "Criminal." The skits recur from album to album, so check the titles carefully when you place them.

The Eminem Show (2002) has 20 tracks and frames itself as a stage production, opening with "Curtains Up (Skit)" and ending with "Curtains Close (Skit)." It includes five skits in total, along with "White America," "Cleanin' Out My Closet," "Without Me" and "'Till I Collapse." The curtain tracks give you the start and finish for free, so the challenge is the middle, where the other skits and the sequence of big songs are easy to mix up.

Take Care (2011) has 18 tracks and a moody, atmospheric sound, with production largely by Noah "40" Shebib. It opens with "Over My Dead Body" and includes "Headlines," "Marvins Room," the Rihanna duet "Take Care," "Crew Love" with The Weeknd, and "Buried Alive Interlude" with Kendrick Lamar. It won the Grammy for Best Rap Album and remains one of the albums people cite most when they talk about Drake's sound. Two interlude-style tracks make it a little trickier than a plain list of songs.

Nothing Was the Same (2013) has 13 tracks and opens with "Tuscan Leather," a long track that changes beats several times. It includes "Started from the Bottom," "Worst Behavior" and "Hold On, We're Going Home," and it closes with "Pound Cake / Paris Morton Music 2," a collaboration with Jay-Z. At 13 tracks it is a manageable length, and the confident, spacious sound makes the singles easy to use as anchors when you rebuild the order.

Views (2016) has 20 tracks and is closely tied to Toronto, the city Drake is from, which appears on the cover and runs through the lyrics. It includes "One Dance," "Controlla," "Pop Style" and "Hotline Bling," and it is a long album that blends rap, R&B and dancehall-influenced songs. With 20 tracks and a steady mid-tempo mood, it is a good test of whether you can keep a long order straight, since many songs sit in a similar emotional range.

Scorpion (2018) has 25 tracks and is widely described as a two-sided album: the first half leans toward rap, and the second half toward R&B. It opens with "Survival," includes "God's Plan," "Nice for What" and "In My Feelings," and the second side begins with "Peak." That split is a useful memory aid, because you only have to decide which half a track belongs to before you place it. It is one of the longer albums in the game, but its structure makes it easier than the number of tracks suggests.

2014 Forest Hills Drive (2014) is named after the address of the house in Fayetteville, North Carolina where J. Cole grew up, and its 13 tracks follow a loose story of growing up and coming home. It was widely noted for having no guest appearances. It begins with "Intro" and includes "Wet Dreamz," "No Role Modelz," "Love Yourz" and "Apparently," before ending with "Note to Self." Because it plays like a story, the order is easier to follow than most hip-hop albums.

Un Verano Sin Ti (2022) has 23 tracks and is built around the mood of a summer, from the opening "Moscow Mule" to the closing "Callaita." It includes "Me Porto Bonito," "Titi Me Preguntó" and "Ojitos Lindos," and it moves between reggaeton, pop and slower, reflective songs. It became the first all-Spanish-language album nominated for Album of the Year at the Grammys. As a long album, it is easier to learn if you divide it into chunks by mood.

YHLQMDLG, short for "Yo Hago Lo Que Me Da La Gana," was released on February 29, 2020 and has 20 tracks. It is a love letter to classic reggaeton and includes "Si Veo a Tu Mamá," "Yo Perreo Sola" and "Safaera," a track famous for shifting through several distinct sections. The album opens with "Si Veo a Tu Mamá" and ends with "<3." Its high energy and varied titles give most tracks a clear identity, which helps when you are rebuilding the order.

Debí Tirar Más Fotos (2025) has 17 tracks and is a tribute to Puerto Rico, drawing on traditional island music alongside reggaeton and electronic sounds. It opens with "Nuevayol," includes "Voy a Llevarte Pa' PR," "Baile Inolvidable," "Turista" and the title track "DtMF," and closes with "La Mudanza." Because it plays as a kind of journey home, the order has a satisfying shape, and with 17 tracks it is a good mid-sized album to try.

album: When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?
text: Billie Eilish's debut album (2019) has 14 tracks and was written and recorded with her brother FINNEAS, largely at home. It opens with a short, odd track titled with a string of exclamation marks, includes "Bad Guy," "Bury a Friend" and "When the Party's Over," and ends with "Goodbye," which briefly revisits fragments of earlier songs. It won the Grammy for Album of the Year in 2020. The bookends make it memorable, but the middle tracks share a similar mood, so they take more practice.

Hit Me Hard and Soft (2024) has just 10 tracks and is designed to be heard from start to finish. It opens with "Skinny," includes "Lunch," "Chihiro" and "Birds of a Feather," and ends with "Blue." With so few songs, there is no filler, and each position carries weight. That makes it an excellent first album for the game: easy to learn, but unforgiving if you swap two tracks that sit close together.

Future Nostalgia (2020) has 11 tracks and is a focused, polished dance-pop album with strong disco and 1980s influences. It opens with its title track and includes "Don't Start Now," "Physical," "Levitating" and "Break My Heart" before finishing with "Boys Will Be Boys." It was released in March 2020, a week earlier than planned. Nearly every track has a clear rhythmic identity and an early hook, so it is one of the easiest albums in the game to rebuild if you know the singles.

Eternal Sunshine (2024) has 13 tracks and shares its title with the 2004 film Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind. It opens with "Intro (End of the World)," places "Saturn Returns Interlude" at track four, and includes "Yes, And?," "We Can't Be Friends (Wait for Your Love)" and "The Boy Is Mine," before ending with "Ordinary Things." The intro and interlude divide it into clear sections, which is useful when you are rebuilding the order from memory.

Thank U, Next (2019) has 12 tracks and was released in February 2019, less than six months after Sweetener. It opens with "Imagine" and includes "7 Rings," "Bad Idea," "Needy" and the title track, and it ends with "Break Up with Your Girlfriend, I'm Bored." The title track and the closer are both singles, which gives you two strong anchors late in the order, so the middle tracks are where you should focus your practice.

Love Yourself: Tear (2018) has 11 tracks and became the first K-pop album to reach number one on the Billboard 200. It opens with "Intro: Singularity" and ends with "Outro: Tear," giving it a clear frame, and includes "Fake Love," "Paradise," "Magic Shop" and "Anpanman." The group moves between rap and singing, and between dance-pop and moodier tracks. The intro and outro make it easy to place the ends, so the challenge is the nine songs in between.

Born Pink (2022) is BLACKPINK's second full-length album and has 8 tracks. It opens with "Pink Venom," followed by "Shut Down," and includes "Typa Girl," "Yeah Yeah Yeah," "Hard to Love," "The Happiest Girl," "Tally" and "Ready for Love." With only eight tracks and two big singles near the front, it is a quick album to learn and a good one for beginners. With so few tracks, even a small mistake shows up right away.
